items.text: The old folks always said words cost nothing; it's just hot air. But that's truly how much I love you. If only you knew.
items.q: Maman quotes an old saying to wave off Ghassem's teasing. Does this sound like her?
before: – Hmm, Ghassem just talks to hear himself talk.

items.text: Now go get some seeds for Ghassem and the others. They want to watch a film.
items.q: Maman means roasted seeds to snack on during the film. Is 'seeds' clear for that?
before: – Hmm, you went there to sightsee and have fun, and you enjoyed yourself. You didn't see any of the hardships.

items.text: Nana-pesar-jan, you really must make sure you eat well. Eat things that build you up. As long as you eat properly, I won't worry about anything else.
items.q: Maman, a mother from a small town, urges her son abroad to eat well. Does it sound like her?
before: – Mm-hm, she'd grown so thin. The last time I went and bathed her, there was no flesh left on her body at all. Just skin and bones. I say if she'd been able to eat, it wouldn't have come to that.

items.text: – Ohhh my. Hmm, the countries must have been close to each other. When was the Bam earthquake?
items.q: Maman hears that one tsunami wave reached fourteen countries. Does her reaction sound natural?
before: – It says its wave reached fourteen countries.
Maman said:

items.text: – It's the end of days. Bibi's generation used to say that when the end of days comes, the earth keeps shaking.
items.q: Maman recalls what her grandmother's generation believed. Does this sound like her?
before: – Ohhh my. Hmm, the countries must have been close to each other. When was the Bam earthquake?
– About a year ago.

items.text: – Goodness, Nini's suddenly feeling sleepy. I've been up since morning and haven't slept.
items.q: Maman, suddenly sleepy, calls herself Nini, the family's affectionate name for her. Does it sound warm and natural?
before: …meter and go. What business is it of yours how much we've used?" Then Baba came back, grumbled a bit, and went to the other house. Nini said, just our luck: Baba's always studying at his place on the other side of the yard, and of course he happened to be here the moment they came for the meter.
Maman presses her eyes shut and says:

items.text: How are you doing? Are you well? Feeling all right? Happy Norouz, Nana-pesar-jan.
items.q: Maman phones her son abroad at Norouz. Does her string of greetings sound warm and natural?

items.text: – Ok, I'm not saying don't fall in love. First get to know the person, get married, and then if you want, fall in love. Then see if I say a word.
items.q: Maman, a mother from a small town, gives her son advice about love. Does it sound like her?
before: In the afternoon, Maman and Omid sat by the open courtyard door so that, as Maman still says, the spring breeze could enter the house and bring freshness. They were drinking tea, and Maman was saying to Omid:

items.text: – Women? I wish he had. Whoever wants him can take him for herself. We'll throw something in on top.
items.q: Maman jokes she would gladly give her husband away. Does 'We'll throw something in on top' sound natural?
before: – What izer wasn't he?
– I mean he didn't chase other women either.

items.text: – Okay, put less. But not too much less. A little less.
items.q: A small boy bargains with his mother over salt on his plums. Does it sound like a small child?
before: – Salt is bad for you.
I said:

items.text: – Stage three is an intersection. An intersection means really big. From this side all the way to that side. From this street to that street.
items.q: Ghassem, a schoolboy leading his little brothers on a pretend mission, says this. Does it sound like a child?
before: On the way he'd say:

items.text: – The left side is dangerous. The house with the red door belongs to a really angry old man. Even angrier than Baba.
items.q: A schoolboy warns his little brothers during their pretend mission. Does it sound like a child?
before: Then he always showed that house with the big red door. He'd say:

items.text: – Hey, why did you throw away the stick? What are we supposed to ring the doorbell with, then?
items.q: Ghassem, a schoolboy, scolds his little brother during their game. Does it sound like a child?
before: I always picked up a stick from beside the tree there. I dragged it along the wall. It made a motorcycle sound. Ghassem and Omid went ahead. I was far behind. Ghassem didn't scold me. One time he said:

items.text: – Beginning of stage one of the mission. Battalion, left turn.
items.q: A schoolboy plays army commander for his little brothers. Does this sound like a child's game?
before: We went into the alley. First we had to go to the start of the alley. Ghassem always said:

items.text: – Going into the main street: tsk-tsk.
items.q: Ghassem, playing commander, forbids going into the busy street. Is 'tsk-tsk' clear as his no?
before: I always do what Maman says. I did what Ghassem said too. He'd say:

items.text: – On the other side of the school is the cemetery. It's really old. Some of the gravestones are gone. You can see the bones of the dead.
items.q: A schoolboy tries to scare his little brothers. Does it sound like a child?
before: I'm going there this year too. If my teacher hits me with a ruler, I'll tell Maman. Ghassem always said:
